column3: Pairs the same "Subhana rabbina" with self-blame, sharpening the response's moral recognition.
Sets speech without enacted reality against the focus's recognition of a promise as enacted.
Uses the exact completed-promise formula within the same surah, giving a concrete precedent for fulfillment.
Extends the preceding confession into hopeful turning toward the Lord, but lacks the focus's fulfillment claim.
Frames the surrounding revelation as arriving in truth and as warning and glad news.
Shows tasbih as rejection of a false attribution, a secondary polemical function beside the focus's reception.
Introduces the recurrent challenge that ties a promise's truth to a demanded timetable.
Completes the immediate scene with tears and increased humility after the voiced tasbih.
Repeats the completed-promise formula in an eschatological setting.
Reprises the timetable challenge, confirming its parallel skeptical posture.
Contrasts desired praise for undone acts with the focus's acknowledgement of an act made real.
Adds collective, ordered tasbih as a communal counterpart to the focus's voiced response.
Supplies another formulation of the timing challenge from a distinct setting.
Provides the contrary model: Satan's promise is explicitly deception, clarifying why fulfillment matters.
Shows a divine promise entering history in stages through an advanced portion.
Adds a humble "rabbana" petition under fear of consequence, parallel to responsive speech.
Explains the deliberate, gradual recitation that immediately precedes the knowledgeable hearers' response.
Offers a contrast route where tasbih disowns false descriptions rather than affirming fulfillment.
Adds a further instance of demanding a date as proof of promise-truth.
Establishes the knowledgeable recipients and their prostration immediately before 17:108.
Contributes a narrower test of whether an asserted agent actually produced an act.
Preserves the recurring demand for a timetable, with little new beyond earlier parallels.
Supplies a remote association/straying frame, not a direct account of the focus's response.
Links remembrance to responsible conduct, reinforcing the word-and-deed contrast.
Adds a believing group's "rabbana" plea as another form of responsive speech.
Extends the surah's reader-accountability bridge from recitation to a personal record.
Offers only a lexical resonance with tasbih, without the focus's reception or promise frame.
Shows both sides finding their Lord's promise true, directly paralleling fulfilled recognition.
Names Satanic promise as deception, a direct contrary reading to the Lord's fulfilled promise.
Adds divine doing as a broad action motif, without a promise or responsive-recitation link.
Presents the unseen promise as actively coming, closely supporting its certain realization.
Continues the surah's accountable-reading thread, but at a different scene and function.
Provides an action-oriented purification motif, only indirectly related to enacted promise.
Adds a "rabbana" response after signs arrive, paralleling reception under pressure.
Begins the channel's warning that visible worldly movement can mislead about eventual outcome.
Adds recorded deeds and accountability, a broad action resonance rather than a focus-specific link.
Restates tasbih as disavowal of human descriptions of the Lord.
Adds public reading of each record, extending the nearby accountability-to-reading bridge.
Stresses effective divine willing and doing, supporting fulfillment at a general level.
Joins the true promise with patience and tasbih, closely paralleling the focus's temporal recognition.
Completes the warning about transient worldly display with its eventual outcome.
Contributes a generic instance of what the Lord did to a past people.
Adds a dependent "rabbana" prayer for protection and forgiveness.
Sets the immediate skeptical demand for a readable book beside the Prophet's tasbih response.
Adds personal acknowledgement of a past deed, only distantly related to fulfilled promise.
Restates tasbih as a reply that invalidates human descriptions of God.
Supplies the corrective to empty speech through faith, deeds, and abundant remembrance.
Adds the recording of what people did, a remote responsibility resonance.
Combines divine choosing with tasbih against association, a secondary theological parallel.
Uses the surah's later-promise arrival, directly placing 17:108 in its promise horizon.
Broadens tasbih into a universal pattern, though not the focus's knowledgeable reception.
Offers a conditional appeal to act, without a clear promise or tasbih connection.
Expands the contrary pattern: deceptive promise leads into commanded distortions and loss.
Shows accusatory fixation on one deed, not a direct reading of fulfilled promise.
Uses tasbih to reject divisive descriptions of deity, a distant secondary parallel.
Uses the same completed-action language for a divine matter brought through altered perception.
Pairs bodily devotion with prolonged tasbih, adding sustained practice rather than fulfillment.
Explicitly contrasts God's true promise with Satan's broken promise after the matter is decided.
Joins the true divine promise to warning against worldly and deceptive assurances.
Names an appointed day, giving the promise a definite horizon of witness and recompense.
Calls the Lord's promise true at its arrival, closely parallel to the focus's certainty.
Matches recited signs with inward increase and trust, directly illuminating receptive hearers.
Links non-hastening before the divine command with tasbih, complementing fulfillment and timing.
Adds praise after grief is removed, a later thankful response rather than promise recognition.
Shows a diseased reading that calls the divine promise deception, preserving the contrary reception.
Uses tasbih to reject unauthorized intercession claims, only secondarily related.
Refines the timing challenge by distinguishing warning-truth from knowledge of its date.
Connects to the focus's tears through the paired divine making of laughter and weeping.
Adds accountable recollection of a wrongful past act, without the promise frame.
Adds a plea invoking a covenant with the Lord, a limited promise-related parallel.
Extends the prior false-promise reading into an attempted retreat justified by a false claim.
Contrasts divine action with human accountability, supporting the action/answer asymmetry.
Supplies return to the Lord, but no direct recitation, tasbih, or promise fulfillment link.
Gives an earlier deception scene that underlies the later contrast with deceptive promises.
Pairs patience under the Lord's judgment with tasbih, supporting sustained response across time.
Presents a promised outcome as an answerable commitment, but not its completed recognition.
Adds confession and a "rabbana" plea after wrongdoing, resonating with 68:29's response.
Affirms that the promised appointment is not broken, a direct but less developed parallel.
Provides a plea to the Lord within punishment, with little connection to the focus's themes.
Shows deception exposed and the Lord's prior warning recalled, clarifying false assurance's outcome.
Offers an anticipated passive consequence, only a general realization motif.
This isolated statement supplies no interpretable addition to the focus without its omitted continuation.
Presents a repeated divine response to wrongdoing, a general enacted-consequence parallel.
Adds a question about an effective human agent, only distantly related to fulfilled promise.
Shows persistent idol devotion, without a direct link to recitation, tasbih, or promise.
Joins tasbih to universal dominion and return, a broad theological counterpart.
Preserves the skeptical demand for timing, though it names an opening rather than the promise.
Adds tasbih joined to acknowledged limits of knowledge, relevant to the knowledgeable hearers' stance.
Supplies communal "rabbana" supplication, but no close promise or recitation relation.
Shows inherited practice substituting for reasons, a remote contrast to tested fulfillment.
Inheritance allocations add no discernible reading of 17:108.
States that what had been promised finally came after extended enjoyment.
The isolated report of disputing adds no focused connection without surrounding speech.
Shows the promise dismissed as ancient tales because of delay, preserving a contrary reception.
The remaining phrase gives no sufficiently specific connection to the focus.
Adds a mutually binding appointment, clarifying that scheduled commitment need not be deceptive.
Contrasts mouth-level profession with absent inward faith and altered speech.
Shows commanded agents acting reliably, a general enactment motif only.
Guidance about gait and voice adds no discernible reading of 17:108.
Joins patience to the true promise while detaching fulfillment from the observer's lifespan.
Sets Satan's threatening promise against God's promise, sharpening the focus's fulfilled-versus-deceptive promise contrast.
Places a "rabbana" address beside certainty that the divine appointment is not broken.
Supplies an explicit historical instance of God fulfilling a promise.
Names God's promise true and contrasts it with unreliable human speech.
Adds a stated divine promise tied to belief and righteous action.
Affirms that what is promised is coming despite human inability to prevent it.
Shows a divine promise entering a concrete historical event, complementing 8:44's completed matter.
Adds a divine promise of enduring outcome for believers.
Calls God's covenantal promise true and asks who fulfills a covenant more completely.
States that God's promise is true while noting that many do not know it.
Presents a specified promise as not to be denied, adding an appointed historical consequence.
Gives a fixed morning appointment, a narrower temporal counterpart to fulfilled promise.
Directly affirms that God does not fail the appointed promise.
Links recognition that God's promise is true with certainty of the Hour.
Closely parallels 17:107-109: recited signs bring prostration and weeping.
Joins tasbih to decisive divine action, supporting the focus's enacted-promise claim.
Names the true promise as drawing near and records the disbelievers' startled recognition.
Affirms the coming Hour as a certain future gathering.
Explicitly denies that God can fail His promise while addressing perceived delay.
Preserves the contrary response that treats a repeated promise as ancient tales.
Gives a divine promise whose realization is described through historical establishment.
Supplies a contrary response to commanded prostration before the All-Merciful.
Uses tasbih to reject an improper claim and to acknowledge dependent worship.
States that God's promise is true as the narrative moves toward its realization.
Presents the divine term as certainly arriving for those who seek the meeting with God.
Explicitly says that God does not fail the promise, while many remain unaware.
Pairs patience with certainty that God's promise is true, closely matching 40:55 and 40:77.
Closely mirrors the focus: reminders produce prostration, tasbih with praise, and humility.
Shows believers recognizing an encountered trial as what God and the Messenger promised, increasing faith and submission.
Supplies a fixed day of appointment that cannot be advanced or delayed.
Joins the truth of God's promise with warning against worldly and deceptive assurances.
Records recognition after awakening that this is what the All-Merciful promised and the messengers confirmed.
Calls the promised divine outcome binding and affirms that God does not fail the appointment.
Depicts tasbih with praise after judgment is decided in truth.
Preserves the contrary reception that calls the true promise and Hour doubtful.
Answers a demand to hasten the threatened matter, extending the timing-challenge pattern.
Identifies an arrived outcome as what had been promised to the responsive and preserving.
Frames the warned consequence as the very day that had been promised.
Preserves the contrast between human perception of the promised day as distant and divine nearness.
Shows the promised reality becoming visible and overturning false assessments of strength.
Maintains the warning that its promised timing is not known to the messenger.
Provides the contrary posture of refusing prostration when the Quran is recited.
Pairs tasbih with prostration among those near the Lord, a broad embodied counterpart.
Uses tasbih to reject descriptions incompatible with divine sovereignty.
Shows tasbih as a response that rejects a grave false claim.
Joins tasbih to the Lord of all worlds within a revelatory encounter.
Commands abundant remembrance, extending the sustained-response dimension of tasbih.
Uses tasbih to reject association while emphasizing divine majesty and dominion.
Shows heavenly bearers of the Throne combining tasbih with faith and intercession.
Pairs heavenly tasbih with praise and intercession for those on earth.
Places tasbih in a voiced recognition of divine enabling after arrival.
Commands tasbih through the night, extending the temporal discipline beside fulfilled promise.
Commands tasbih of the great Lord in a context of divine power and accountability.
Ends with tasbih of the great Lord as a concluding recognition of certain realities.
Adds universal tasbih under divine might and wisdom.
Adds universal tasbih under divine might and wisdom.
Adds universal tasbih under divine might, wisdom, and messengerly recitation.
Adds universal tasbih with divine power over all things.
Commands tasbih of the great Lord after a declared certain reality.
Commands tasbih of the Most High Lord, a concise liturgical parallel.
Joins tasbih with praise and seeking forgiveness at the arrival of divine help.
